rationale: The claimant's own property (kitchen cabinets, ceiling, and walls) sustained fire and smoke damage from a kitchen accident at their own home, with no third-party involvement or motor vehicle involved.
claim_summary: Policy POL-1001 (Alex Doe, homeowners, active, $250,000 limit, $500 deductible). Incident: Kitchen fire yesterday evening caused by grease flare-up while sauteing onions; claimant extinguished with fire extinguisher. Damage: Charred kitchen cabinets above stove, smoke damage to ceiling and walls; rest of house unaffected. No injuries. Classification: Property damage (confidence 1.0). Severity: Medium—moderate property loss requiring professional restoration, localized to kitchen.

case_facts.description: stove fire caused by grease flare-up while sauteing onions; extinguished with fire extinguisher
case_facts.damage: charred kitchen cabinets above stove; smoke damage on ceiling and walls; rest of house unaffected

rationale: Water damage to the claimant's own property (hardwood floor, drywall, stored items) caused by a malfunction of the claimant's own plumbing system (burst bathroom supply line), clearly falls within property damage coverage.
claim_summary: Policy POL-1004 (Homeowners Premium, active, $750,000 limit, $500 deductible) held by Sam Patel. Claim: Basement flooded with approximately 2 inches of water caused by burst supply line under upstairs bathroom sink that ran for approximately 2 days while claimant was on work trip. Damage includes buckled hardwood floor, water-soaked drywall up to 1 foot high, and ruined stored boxes. Classification: Property Damage (confidence 0.95). Severity: High—extensive structural damage, significant property loss, and extended water exposure indicates substantial remediation costs.

case_facts.damage_description: hardwood floor buckled, drywall soaked up to about 1 foot high, stored boxes ruined
case_facts.discovery_context: claimant returned from work trip to find water
case_facts.water_source: burst supply line under upstairs bathroom sink, ran for approximately two days

rationale: Wind-caused loss of roof shingles to the claimant's own property is straightforward property damage with no involvement of third parties or liability.
claim_summary: Policyholder: Jordan Lee (POL-1006, homeowners premium, active). Incident: Wind damage last weekend removed four shingles from back porch roof overhang. No water intrusion or secondary damage. Estimated repair cost: $400. Policy has $1,000,000 coverage limit with $2,500 deductible. Claim classified as property_damage with high confidence (0.95) and low severity due to minor isolated damage and modest cost.
